summary:
"Saúde em Órbita" (Health in Orbit) is a proposed integrated platform for monitoring and tracking the health of astronauts during space missions. The project combines a biomedical tracking application with a system designed to integrate with wearable sensors embedded in spacesuits, enabling the monitoring of indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, blood glucose levels, sleep quality, and emotional state.

Using a visual interface that features an anatomical representation of the human body and color-coded indicators, the system presents health information intuitively; it also provides guidance and tracks data trends throughout the mission. The proposal further includes offline functionality, multilingual accessibility, a biometric history log, and gamification features to encourage healthy habits.

The goal is to enhance astronaut autonomy, facilitate the early detection of physiological changes, and contribute to human safety and well-being during long-duration space missions.
details:
Solution Functionality and Architecture

"Saúde em Órbita" (Health in Orbit) was conceived as a biomedical monitoring platform integrated with wearable devices, designed to be coupled with spacesuits and used inside space stations.

The application features an anatomical representation of the astronaut, allowing for the visualization of various physiological systems and indicators through a color-coded system. It employs three visual levels—blue, yellow, and red—to represent different health monitoring and attention statuses.

Monitored parameters include heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, blood glucose levels, sleep quality, and emotional state. The system also includes supplementary features for recording images, videos, and medical test results, providing accessible guidance to assist the astronaut in data collection.

Data Monitoring and Analysis

The platform organizes biomedical data into a longitudinal history, enabling the tracking of physiological changes from the beginning to the end of a mission. Time-series graphs allow for the observation of trends and the identification of potential shifts in health indicators.

The proposal incorporates intelligent data analysis to identify patterns and potential anomalies, issue alerts, and provide guidance in plain, simple language. In critical situations, the system can support decision-making and facilitate communication with medical teams on Earth.

Autonomy and Accessibility

Given the connectivity limitations and operational conditions of the space environment, the project is designed for offline functionality, local data storage, and operational autonomy in the event of station instability.

The interface is designed for accessibility, offering multilingual support, subtitles, audiovisual features, and sign language (Libras) integration. It also includes physical exercise guidance adapted to the astronaut's specific environment.

Another key feature is gamification—incorporating levels, points, and medals—to encourage health tracking and the maintenance of healthy habits. Innovation and Intended Impact

The key differentiator of "Saúde em Órbita" (Health in Orbit) is its integration of physiological monitoring, anatomical visualization, longitudinal tracking, and health support into a single platform—prioritizing astronaut autonomy and ensuring that information is easy to interpret.

The solution aims to contribute to the prevention of biomedical risks, the early identification of physiological changes, and the safety of crews during long-duration space missions.

Tools and Development

The project includes a conceptual interface prototype developed in Canva, which serves to illustrate the visual experience and the organization of the application’s features.

Integration with wearable biomedical sensors, intelligent analysis mechanisms, universal data storage, and energy autonomy solutions are all part of the proposed technological architecture and represent avenues for future development.

The team identifies the following as fundamental requirements: data reliability, accessibility, information security, energy autonomy, sustainability, and ease of use in extreme space environments.
